# MASTER DEVELOPMENT PROMPT: INCLUSIVE UNIVERSITY SYSTEM

Act as a senior full-stack software engineer, UI/UX designer, and system architect.

I am developing an **Inclusive University System**, a modern university learning platform initially targeting Kirinyaga University, Kenya, with plans to expand to other universities.

Your task is to analyse my existing project, redesign its entire user interface, and implement the features described below.

Do not simply generate a landing page or static prototype. Build a functional, responsive learning management platform.

## 1. First: Analyse the Existing Project

Before making changes:

- Inspect the existing codebase, pages, components, and architecture.
- Identify existing features that can be retained.
- Identify incomplete features and areas requiring improvement.
- Preserve working functionality.
- Avoid unnecessary duplication of components.
- Do not remove existing data or working integrations.
- Establish a consistent design system before implementing the new layout.

## 2. New UI/UX Design

Completely redesign the interface to look like a premium, modern educational technology platform.

Design direction:
- Clean, modern, professional, and minimal.
- A polished dashboard with a clear visual hierarchy.
- Consistent typography, spacing, icons, and colours.
- Responsive design for desktop, tablets, and mobile phones.
- Smooth transitions and subtle animations.
- Intuitive navigation with minimal clutter.
- Accessible interface with readable text and clear controls.

### Student dashboard layout

Create a dashboard containing:

- Welcome message with student's name.
- Profile information and academic details.
- Current semester.
- Enrolled courses.
- Recently accessed learning materials.
- Learning progress overview.
- Upcoming assignments and deadlines.
- Recent quiz results.
- Recommended learning resources.
- Quick access to continue reading.

Use a modern sidebar navigation on desktop and an appropriate mobile navigation system.

## 3. Student Features

### A. Authentication and profiles
- Student registration and login.
- Secure authentication.
- Student profile management.
- University, programme, year of study, and semester information.
- Password reset functionality.
- Role-based access control.

### B. Academic structure

Organize academic content using this hierarchy:

University → Faculty/School → Programme → Academic Year → Semester → Unit → Topic → Learning Material.

Students should be able to navigate this structure easily.

Initially support Kirinyaga University, but design the architecture to accommodate multiple universities.

### C. Interactive learning environment

This is one of the most important features.

Students must be able to read learning materials directly on the platform rather than being forced to download PDFs.

Implement:

- An in-browser PDF and document reader.
- Structured topic-based notes.
- Previous and next topic navigation.
- Table of contents.
- Search within learning materials where supported.
- Adjustable reading experience.
- Bookmarking and saving important topics.
- Download functionality where permitted.
- A clear indication of reading progress.

The reading interface should be distraction-free and comfortable for extended study sessions.

### D. Interactive quizzes

Integrate quizzes directly into the learning experience.

After completing a topic, students should be able to attempt related questions.

Implement:
- Multiple-choice questions.
- True/false questions.
- Short-answer questions where appropriate.
- Automatic marking for supported question types.
- Immediate feedback.
- Correct answers and explanations.
- Quiz scores.
- Quiz attempt history.
- Retakes according to configurable rules.

Quizzes should feel like part of the learning process, not a separate disconnected application.

### E. Learning progress tracking

Create a student progress dashboard showing:

- Topics completed.
- Topics not yet completed.
- Units being studied.
- Quiz performance.
- Average scores.
- Learning activity history.
- Overall course progress.

Use progress bars and meaningful visualizations.

Students should be able to continue from where they stopped reading.

### F. Search and discovery

Create a global search feature that allows students to find:

- Units.
- Topics.
- Lecture notes.
- Learning resources.
- Quizzes.

Include filtering by programme, year, semester, and unit.

## 4. Administration Dashboard

Create a separate administration interface.

Administrators should be able to:

- Manage universities.
- Manage faculties and programmes.
- Create academic years and semesters.
- Create and manage units.
- Upload learning materials.
- Organize notes into topics.
- Create and manage quizzes.
- Review submitted resources.
- Approve or reject submitted content.
- Manage students and contributors.
- View platform activity.
- Manage reported incorrect or outdated materials.

Include a content approval workflow.

Only authorized administrators should be able to publish approved learning materials.

## 5. Lecturer and Contributor Features

Create appropriate permissions for lecturers and approved contributors.

They should be able to:

- Submit learning materials.
- Associate materials with the correct units.
- Organize materials into topics.
- Create quiz questions where authorized.
- Edit their submissions.
- View approval status.
- Receive feedback when content is rejected.

Submitted materials must be reviewed before publication.

## 6. Accessibility and Inclusion

The platform must genuinely support inclusive learning.

Implement:

- Responsive mobile-first design.
- Readable fonts and appropriate contrast.
- Keyboard-friendly navigation.
- Accessible form labels and controls.
- Screen-reader-friendly page structures.
- Captions for video content where available.
- Downloadable resources where permitted.
- Lightweight pages suitable for students with limited internet connectivity.

Do not rely on colour alone to communicate important information.

## 7. Database and Backend Architecture

Design a scalable relational database.

Include appropriate entities for:

- Universities.
- Faculties.
- Programmes.
- Academic years.
- Semesters.
- Units.
- Topics.
- Students.
- Lecturers.
- Administrators.
- Learning resources.
- Quizzes.
- Questions.
- Answers.
- Quiz attempts.
- Student progress.
- Bookmarks.
- Content submissions.
- Content approvals.
- Notifications.

Establish appropriate relationships, primary keys, foreign keys, and data validation.

Ensure student records and learning progress are protected by proper authorization policies.

## 8. Technical Requirements

Use the existing project's technology stack where practical.

If the project needs a suitable stack, prefer:

- Frontend: Next.js, React, and TypeScript.
- Styling: Tailwind CSS.
- UI components: shadcn/ui.
- Backend and database: Supabase and PostgreSQL.
- Authentication: Supabase Auth.
- File storage: Supabase Storage.
- PDF viewing: PDF.js or an equivalent solution.
- Version control: Git and GitHub.
- Deployment: Vercel.

Do not introduce unnecessary technologies or replace working integrations without justification.

## 9. Important Design Requirements

The system must have two clearly separated experiences:

**Student experience:** Focused on discovering courses, reading notes, practising quizzes, and tracking learning progress.

**Administration experience:** Focused on managing academic structures, users, content, quizzes, and approvals.

Both interfaces must use the same overall design language while serving different purposes.

## 10. Development and Testing Instructions

Implement features in logical modules.

For every feature:

- Build the actual interface.
- Connect it to the backend where applicable.
- Implement validation and error handling.
- Include loading, empty, and success states.
- Test the main user workflows.
- Ensure navigation and buttons perform their intended actions.
- Avoid fake functionality and placeholder interactions.

If backend credentials or integrations are unavailable, clearly identify what is needed rather than pretending the feature works.

## 11. Final Objective

The final product should be a polished, functional, inclusive university learning platform that improves the traditional university portal experience.

Take inspiration from existing LMS platforms such as Kirinyaga University's Masomo Portal, but do not simply copy its appearance.

Our goal is to create a better learning experience through:

1. Organized academic resources.
2. Seamless online reading.
3. Interactive quizzes.
4. Instant learning feedback.
5. Personal learning progress.
6. Accessible and inclusive design.
7. Scalable multi-university architecture.

**Development priority:** Start with the redesigned student dashboard, academic navigation, online reading experience, and interactive quizzes. Then implement progress tracking, administration, content management, and advanced features.

Build a cohesive product, not a collection of disconnected pages.

## NEW FEATURE: INTERACTIVE WEB-BASED STUDY NOTES

Implement a dedicated study-notes reading experience.

The system must display academic notes as properly formatted web content rather than displaying every document as a PDF.

### 1. Notes presentation

When a student opens a unit or topic, display the notes directly inside the platform.

Support:
- Structured topic headings and subheadings.
- Numbered sections and subsections.
- Bold and italic text.
- Bullet points and numbered lists.
- Properly formatted tables.
- Mathematical equations and formulas.
- Images, illustrations, and diagrams.
- Code blocks for programming subjects.
- Definitions and highlighted important concepts.
- Examples and explanations.
- Revision questions and examination questions.

### 2. Reading interface

Create a professional academic reading layout with:

- A left sidebar containing the unit's table of contents.
- A central reading area containing the notes.
- A right sidebar for bookmarks, important concepts, or learning progress where appropriate.
- Previous and next topic navigation.
- Reading progress indicator.
- Search within the notes.
- Responsive mobile layout.

### 3. Interactive learning

Allow students to:
- Highlight important text.
- Bookmark sections.
- Take personal notes.
- Mark topics as completed.
- Answer revision questions.
- Reveal answers and explanations.
- Continue reading from their previous position.

### 4. Content management

Administrators and approved contributors must be able to create and edit notes using a rich-text editor.

The editor should support:
- Headings and subheadings.
- Tables.
- Images.
- Equations.
- Lists.
- Code blocks.
- Links.
- Embedded diagrams.

Store notes in a structured format in the database rather than treating all content as PDF files.

Allow administrators to import existing documents and convert or organize their content into editable web-based notes. Imported content must be reviewed before publication.

### 5. PDF support

PDF files should remain supported as supplementary downloadable resources.

However, the primary reading experience must be the native web-based notes interface.

### 6. Academic content organization

Follow this hierarchy:

University → Programme → Year → Semester → Unit → Topic → Notes.

### 7. Design reference

Use the Software Quality Assurance study notes format as a content-presentation reference:

- Clear topic numbering.
- Strong heading hierarchy.
- Readable paragraphs.
- Well-formatted tables.
- Proper mathematical notation.
- Organized revision questions.
- Consistent spacing.

Do not reproduce the exact visual design. Create a modern, polished academic reading experience.

**Core requirement: Students must be able to study complete, properly formatted lecture notes directly on the website without needing to open or download a PDF.**
